definitions.explanation: the amount of water contained in food, fabric, or other materials

examples.japanese: {野菜|やさい}の{水気|みずけ}を{切|き}る。
examples.english: Drain the moisture from the vegetables.

examples.japanese: キッチンペーパーで{水気|みずけ}を{拭|ふ}き{取|と}った。
examples.english: I wiped off the moisture with a paper towel.

examples.japanese: {肉|にく}を{焼|や}く{前|まえ}に、しっかり{水気|みずけ}を{取|と}っておくと{美味|おい}しく{焼|や}ける。
examples.english: If you remove the moisture thoroughly before cooking meat, it will brown nicely.

notes:
{水気|みずけ} refers to the moisture or water content in food or other materials, commonly used in cooking contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水気|みずけ}を{切|き}る (to drain moisture)
- {水気|みずけ}を{取|と}る (to remove moisture)
- {水気|みずけ}を{拭|ふ}く (to wipe off moisture)
- {水気|みずけ}が{多|おお}い (has a lot of moisture)

COOKING USAGE:
- Essential term in recipes, especially when preparing salads or frying
- Removing {水気|みずけ} before frying prevents oil splatter
- For salads, draining {水気|みずけ} prevents watery dressing

RELATED TERMS:
- {水分|すいぶん} (moisture content - more formal/scientific)
- {湿気|しっけ} (humidity, dampness in the air)
- {潤|うるお}い (moisture - positive nuance, often for skin)
